transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-03-16
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 min
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Samira Gupta (Redwood SE), Sara Malik (RiverMark Dir. ML), Tom Rivera (Infra), Priya Nair (CTO)

Auto-generated Summary: Reviewed TTFT and p95 numbers from last week's runs; discussed streaming chunking and kernel tradeoffs; agreed on next microbenchmarks and owners.

Topics: TTFT, streaming behaviour, max sequence tuning, kernel choice, pre-warm/pinning, KV cache.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, morning, quick check — we have 45 minutes on the agenda: go over the latest bench, dig into TTFT and streaming, then action items.
[00:18] Sara: yep thanks Ethan, excited to see the numbers. we ran your script overnight and have the logs up, just a heads up some of the timestamps are a bit off in our side but should be fine.
[00:30] Samira: quick note, i pulled p50/p95 from the run you shared: p50 ~ 120ms first token for the 7B quant, p95 ~ 640ms, overall token throughput looks ok but TTFT is above our 100ms target.
[00:48] Tom: our tail latency matters cause of SLAs, and a lot of our requests are bursty with long sequences occasionally. we saw a spike around 1024 tokens for a few requests.
[01:05] Ethan: understood. on the run we did two variants: streaming enabled with 64-token chunks and non-streaming. TTFT was worse with larger chunks — streaming helps but first token still suffers if the runtime waits for a chunk.
[01:30] Priya: can you remind us how the streaming chunking is implemented? is it on the Redwood side or client-side chunking?
[01:40] Samira: it's runtime-level chunking — we stream partial outputs once the model emits a chunk; but TTFT depends on tokenization and kernel warm paths; if the kernel path needs to initialize or we hit a cold kv cache, that adds ~50-150ms.
[02:00] Sara: we also saw variability across regions, but this POC is on Dedicated in us-west only. are there kernel options we can toggle? we use the default compiled kernel.
[02:12] Ethan: yes — we can swap kernel backends: flash-attn (fast for short sequences), tiled kernel (better memory pattern for longer sequences), and a fallback slower kernel. Samira has the comparison notes.
[02:30] Samira: right, in our internal bench flash-attn gave best p50 for seq<=256, tiled began to shine >512, and for 1024+ we recommend tiled or enabling KV cache optimizations; also quantization profile matters — 4-bit quant with per-channel remap had slightly higher TTFT on first token.
[02:58] Tom: so for us, our seq distribution is bimodal: 70% under 128, 20% 256-512, and 10% 512-1024. that should guide kernel choice.
[03:15] Ethan: that distribution is helpful — suggests we should bias for flash-attn for the common case and have auto-fallback to tiled for long seq. we can do policy-based routing per request size.
[03:34] Sara: what about pre-warm / pinning? we saw a cold start TTL causing some bursts.
[03:42] Samira: pre-warm helps a lot for TTFT — pin a worker with kernel loaded, keep a warm KV cache for hot prefixes. There's a memory cost but reduces first-token by ~80-120ms in our tests.
[04:00] Priya: are there security implications for pinning on Dedicated? we need to ensure isolation.
[04:08] Ethan: on Dedicated we can pin within customer-only pools; it still respects KMS, RBAC, and audit logs. we'll share the security doc.
[04:20] Sara: can you run a microbenchmark for us: enable flash-attn, streaming chunk 32, max seq 256 and then tiled + chunk 64 with max seq 1024? we want the delta and also the TTFT numbers.
[04:36] Samira: yes we can. for clarity we'll run three configs: A) flash-attn, chunk 32, seq cap 256; B) tiled, chunk 64, seq cap 1024; C) flash-attn with pre-warm and pinned worker.
[04:50] Tom: and include tokenization overhead and network RTT in the numbers please — our infra adds about 20ms average.
[05:00] Ethan: noted. quick walk-through of last bench: the run on 7B q4_0 (approx) showed TTFT p50 120ms p95 640ms; enabling streaming with chunk 32 reduced p95 to ~420ms but TTFT only marginally improved. pre-warm reduced TTFT to ~40-60ms p50 in a follow-up quick test.
[05:28] Sara: interesting — so pre-warm is the low-hanging fruit. what's the memory cost?
[05:36] Samira: roughly one worker pinned per concurrent slot; depends on model size. for 7B quant it's moderate but for 13B it's larger. we'll estimate exact GB in the sheet.
[05:50] Ethan: also want to call out batching tradeoffs: increasing batch size reduces per-token cost but increases TTFT; for interactive use we keep small batches or enable immediate partial decode.
[06:10] Priya: what about KV cache strategies? we don't always have prefix caching possible because requests are varied.
[06:20] Samira: KV caching helps when there's repetition or multi-turn chat; for single-shot it's less beneficial. For your workload (mostly single-shot short queries) caching helps little, so optimize for TTFT rather than cache hits.
[06:38] Tom: we plan to trim prompts server-side to reduce seq length; do you have heuristics?
[06:45] Ethan: yes, pre-token trimming (drop low-value context), use compressed system prompts, and prioritize immediate user text. we can share a heuristics doc and sample code.
[06:58] Sara: can we test aggressive trimming to move more requests into <=128?
[07:04] Samira: absolutely, we'll include a trimmed-run in the microbench.
[07:10] Ethan: okay next, kernel switch mechanics — Samira can do a canary: route 10% of requests through flash-attn with streaming 32 and measure. if metrics look good ramp to 50.
[07:25] Samira: yes we'll prepare the canary config in the rollout system; it supports per-model and per-route rules.
[07:33] Priya: timeline — we want to see results within a week to decide whether to go Dedicated pilot or stay hosted. what do you recommend?
[07:42] Ethan: if we hit TTFT <100ms p50 and p95 <500ms with the flash-attn + pre-warm + trimmed prompts, Dedicated pilot looks viable. otherwise we iterate on kernels/quant.
[07:55] Sara: any gotchas with quantization? we saw minor quality drop with q4 on some eval prompts.
[08:03] Samira: correct — q4 has occasional hallucination on certain prompt types, we recommend running your eval set; Redwood Optimize can run quality regressions against the prompt set and flag issues.
[08:18] Tom: can you share the Optimize eval pipeline? we'd like to run it against our 200 prompt eval set.
[08:24] Ethan: yes will share link and instructions; we'll also upload a small harness for automated runs.
[08:33] Sara: ok plan sounds good. also please include the OS/kernel versions and exact runtime builds used in bench results we got — there were some mismatches in our environments.
[08:44] Samira: noted, we'll put runtime build, kernel flags, and compile options in the sheet.
[08:52] Ethan: to recap action items — (a) Ethan: share dashboard + bench sheet (b) Samira: kernel comparison + canary config (c) Tom: provide seq length distribution and network RTT samples (d) Priya: security contact for Dedicated pilot. agreed?
[09:10] Sara: agreed.
[09:15] Priya: agreed.
[09:18] Tom: agreed.
[09:20] Ethan: cool — we'll aim for microbench results mid-week and a kernel deep-dive Tue/Thu next week. if the customer completes their internal run we'll meet again same time next week for results review.
[09:35] Sara: one more quick Q: does Redwood have autotune for chunk size?
[09:40] Samira: there is an experimental autotune that monitors TTFT vs p95 and recommends chunk size; we'll enable it behind a flag for the canary so you can test.
[09:52] Sara: perfect. thanks everyone.
[09:56] Ethan: thanks all, end.

End of transcript.
